system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Bottom line

The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every material point. Several departures reinforce each other, so the combined effect is much worse than any single change. Read together, clauses 12.1–12.3, 9.3/12.8/20.5, 8.3 and the general disclosure in the Disclosure Letter would leave us with:

- a reduced cap;
- thresholds high enough to screen out most claims;
- a shorter claims window;
- no separate protection for title;
- no fraud carve-out; and
- every risk in the data room treated as disclosed and known to us.

That last point covers Bluefen, Riverlark, the bonuses, Ironquay and DD-006, which are exactly the risks the specific protections are meant to address.

The cover email calls the package "fair and balanced", and a footnote at the end of the Disclosure Letter says all positions are "standard market terms" to be accepted without objection. Under playbook sec 0.4/6.3 these are counterparty assertions, not verified facts or cleared positions. I have not relied on them. The footnote is unusual in a disclosure document, and it is worth asking Seller's counsel to remove it from the final version.

---

## 1. Liability regime

**1.1 General cap: clause 12.1 proposes 20% / AUD 4.8m. Reject and hold at 25% / AUD 6.0m.**
- 20% matches our conditional fallback, but that fallback needs prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft. None has been given.
- A matching number does not make the change cleared. Do not concede it or signal that it is available.
- If the team wants to use the fallback, get Amelia's written authority first and trade it for something, such as the threshold or fraud points.

**1.2 Thresholds: clause 12.2 proposes AUD 25,000 de minimis and AUD 250,000 basket, deductible only. Reject; counter at AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000, tipping from the first dollar.**
- Both figures are five times our position.
- Switching from a tipping basket to a deductible ("only the excess") permanently removes AUD 250,000 of recovery even for valid claims.
- A AUD 25,000 de minimis would exclude many individual data-handling, contract and employee items.

**1.3 Time limits: clause 12.3/13 proposes 18 months. Reject; hold at 24 months.**
- 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written approval. None has been given.

**1.4 The "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" sweep-up (clause 12.3/13). Reject outright.**
- This is the hidden general-regime override the playbook warns about.
- It would quietly apply the general cap, thresholds and time limit to title, capacity, tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenant claims.
- Each category must keep its own regime. Limitations should apply only to the categories they expressly name.

**1.5 Fundamental and title warranties put into the general regime "for administrative simplicity". Reject.**
- Title and capacity warranties go to whether we actually acquire 100% of the shares.
- Our position:
  - a separate regime;
  - a 100% cap (AUD 24m);
  - a claims period of at least six years; and
  - outside the basket, the de minimis and any knowledge bar.
- "Administrative simplicity" does not justify capping title exposure at 20%.

**1.6 Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature". Reject. This is a red line.**
- As drafted there is no carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct.
- These must sit outside all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- The playbook states that no one may waive this. It is not a trading point.

---

## 2. Disclosure and knowledge

**2.1 General disclosure (Disclosure Letter paras 1.1 and 1.2). Reject.**
- Para 1.1 discloses the whole data room, including DD-002 to DD-012.
- Para 1.2 discloses the Accounts, the statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records".
- Together these would make every documented issue a disclosed matter and defeat warranty claims on it.
- Require specific fair disclosure only. Each disclosure must identify the warranty it qualifies and describe the matter in enough detail for us to assess its nature and scope.
- The "without limiting any specific disclosure" wording in para 1.2 does not help us; it only preserves the Seller's general disclosure on top of the specific items.

**2.2 Buyer knowledge (clause 8.3). Delete.**
- The clause covers our advisers' knowledge and anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records. That is constructive knowledge with no limit.
- It also duplicates and amplifies the general disclosure.
- If any qualifier survives, it must:
  - be limited to the actual knowledge of named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry; and
  - never excuse title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

**2.3 Para 1.4 non-admission.** Acceptable in principle. It must not be used to dilute the factual accuracy of the specific disclosures.

---

## 3. Deal-specific issues

**3.1 Bluefen consent (clause 3/6.3; DD-002). Major issue. Reject.**
- Bluefen is roughly AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue, about 30% of the business.
- The Seller offers "reasonable endeavours" and treats the condition as satisfied once the counterparty's written consent is delivered.
- Para 2 of the Disclosure Letter confirms there is no final consent and no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- Require a Completion condition that is satisfied only when:
  - an effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) Bluefen consent is obtained; and
  - documentary evidence shows the clause 11.3 conditions are met before Completion.
- The Seller's statement that the consent "is addressed" is an assertion, not a fact.

**3.2 Riverlark facility (clause 2/7; DD-003, approx. AUD 3.2m). Reject the post-Completion release.**
- The facility has not been repaid, and no discharge is in the data room (para 3).
- The facility contains a change-control clause (8.1), so Completion may itself trigger default.
- Require:
  - a current payout letter;
  - repayment directly from Completion funds as a funds-flow line item, deducted from price on our debt-free basis; and
  - executed, effective security releases delivered at Completion (deeds of release, PPSR discharges and any share security released).
- A post-Completion release is a fallback only. It needs an irrevocable lender undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval, neither of which we have.
- Confirm the outstanding figure: "approximately" is not good enough for a payout.

**3.3 Employee bonuses (DD-005, AUD 420,000). Reject the silent exclusion.**
- The Seller says the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller", yet they are not in the funds flow.
- The Company is the employer and will bear the liability after Completion.
- On-costs (payroll tax, superannuation, possibly PAYG and workers' compensation) are unaddressed. Para 5 says the letter does not state whether they apply.
- Require either:
  - a specific funds-flow line item covering AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs, treated as Debt or Transaction Expense; or
  - Seller funding, backed by a specific indemnity outside the general regime.

**3.4 Ironquay IP (clause 11.1; DD-004/DD-010). Broaden the indemnity.**
- The current indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment.
- The real risk is that SOW3 Project Materials do not transfer: clause 7.3 makes transfer conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee, and there is no confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- Broaden the indemnity to cover:
  - failure to obtain title to or rights in the Project Materials;
  - third-party IP claims; and
  - costs of replacement or remediation.
- Preserve the SOW3 cure by requiring, as a Completion deliverable or pre-Completion covenant, payment plus a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay.
- The AUD 180,000 open amount comes from DD-010 and is not independently verified either way. Do not assume it is owed or that it has been paid. Ask for bank and payment evidence.

**3.5 DD-006 export/privacy incident (clause 4.6/Schedule 6). Reject the characterisation.**
- The Seller calls it "not expected to be material". That is an unsupported assertion.
- The Disclosure Letter itself says access, scope and any notification duty are unknown and the investigation is preliminary.
- We should not overstate the incident either. There is no confirmed breach, harm, notification obligation or quantified loss.
- Require covenants to:
  - preserve all logs and evidence;
  - complete a proper investigation, including access logs for the link and the scope of roughly 1,240 records;
  - give regular written updates before Completion; and
  - consult us on any regulator or individual notification decision.
- Reserve the right to seek a specific indemnity once the facts are clearer. Take no numeric position now.

**3.6 Sandbar renewals (DD-008/DD-011, AUD 330,000). Do not accept "ordinary course" as stated.**
- The Disclosure Letter itself (para 8) says it does not state whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
- The three related renewals should be read together for timing.
- Request the contracts, termination rights and accrual treatment, then assess.
- Equally, do not automatically classify them as Debt or demand a price deduction. Our position stays open pending that review.

**3.7 Tax and IP (Seller says "settled under the general regime"). Reject.**
- Both remain OPEN on our side. Nothing has been resolved.
- They must keep separate categories and must not fall into the general regime through the clause 12.3 sweep-up.
- Do not assume unlimited liability either way.

**3.8 Title evidence (DD-012). Insufficient.**
- DD-012 is the Company's own internal register. Para 10 confirms it is the Seller's source and not our verification.
- Require independent evidence:
  - a current ASIC company extract;
  - share certificates or a holding statement;
  - PPSR and encumbrance searches over the shares and the Company, which links to Riverlark security;
  - Seller board authority and capacity; and
  - confirmation that there are no options, convertibles or rights to issue shares.

**3.9 Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009). Lower priority.**
- On the Seller's description, these involve a notification obligation and an assignment restriction that the share sale does not trigger.
- Have our team read the provisions directly to confirm there is no change-of-control trigger.
- Add any required notice to the Completion deliverables or covenants.

---

## 4. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | Hold at 25% / AUD 6.0m. No fallback without Amelia Frost's written authority. |
| 2 | Thresholds | AUD 25k / AUD 250k, deductible | AUD 5k / AUD 50k, tipping from the first dollar |
| 3 | Claims period | 18 months | 24 months. No fallback without written approval. |
| 4 | "Applies to all Claims" | Sweep-up | Delete. Keep categories separate. |
| 5 | Title/capacity | General regime | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket and knowledge bar |
| 6 | Fraud | No carve-out | Full carve-out from all limitations. Red line. |
| 7 | Disclosure | Whole data room and public records | Specific fair disclosure only |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket, constructive | Delete. Any qualifier limited to named persons plus reasonable enquiry, never excusing title, fraud or indemnities. |
| 9 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours, consent on delivery | Effective consent plus evidence of clause 11.3 conditions as a CP before Completion |
| 10 | Riverlark | Post-Completion release | Payout letter, direct repayment from funds, releases at Completion |
| 11 | Bonuses | Excluded from funds flow | Line item including on-costs, or Seller-funded with indemnity |
| 12 | Ironquay | Narrow SOW3-payment indemnity | Broaden to IP and transfer failure. Preserve SOW3 cure. Verify the AUD 180k. |
| 13 | DD-006 | "Not material" | Log preservation, investigation and update covenants. No assumptions either way. |
| 14 | Sandbar | "Ordinary course" | Request documents and assess. No automatic Debt treatment. |
| 15 | Tax/IP | "Settled" | Open. Separate categories. |
| 16 | Title evidence | DD-012 register | Independent ASIC, PPSR, certificate and authority evidence |

**Suggested priorities for the mark-up:**
1. The fraud carve-out (non-negotiable), the title regime and deletion of the sweep-up.
2. Disclosure and buyer knowledge, because without these fixes every other protection is hollow.
3. The Bluefen CP, the Riverlark payout and the bonus funds-flow line. These are each Completion mechanics with seven-figure or 30%-revenue exposure.
4. The cap, thresholds and time limit at our starting positions.

If the team wants flexibility on the cap or claims period, the next step is to seek Amelia Frost's written authority identifying this draft (SPA-003 / Seller Update) before signalling anything to the Seller.
=== END ADVICE ===
